claim: In the Drosophila embryo, neural progenitors (neuroblasts; NBs) produce a sequence of unique neurons whose identities depend on the sequential expression of temporal transcription factors (TTFs).
source: In the Drosophila embryo, neural progenitors (neuroblasts; NBs) produce a sequence of unique neurons whose identities depend on the sequential expression of temporal transcription factors (TTFs).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of Drosophila developmental biology, as indicated by the context of the manuscript.

claim: The TTF timer is commonly described as a relay of activators.
source: The TTF timer is commonly described as a relay of activators, but its regulatory circuit is also consistent with a repressor-decay timer, where TTF expression begins when its repressor decays.
evidence: This is supported by citations to existing literature describing the TTF timer mechanism.

claim: The TTF regulatory circuit is also consistent with a repressor-decay timer, where TTF expression begins when its repressor decays.
source: The TTF timer is commonly described as a relay of activators, but its regulatory circuit is also consistent with a repressor-decay timer, where TTF expression begins when its repressor decays.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the regulatory circuit structure and inference from known interactions.

claim: Repressor-decay timers are more robust to parameter variations than activator-relay timers.
source: Theory shows that repressor-decay timers are more robust to parameter variations than activator-relay timers.
evidence: This is supported by theoretical modeling and computational analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: The TTF sequence progresses primarily by repressor-decay.
source: Comparing WT and mutant NBs at high temporal resolution, we show that the TTF sequence progresses primarily by repressor-decay.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing wild-type and mutant embryos.

claim: Biological timers synchronize patterning processes during embryonic development.
source: Biological timers synchronize patterning processes during embryonic development.
evidence: This is established knowledge in developmental biology.

claim: Temporal coordination is often achieved through cell-autonomous processes that measure time-delays.
source: By contrast, temporal coordination is often achieved through cell-autonomous processes that measure time-delays (Pourquié, 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Biological timers play a key role in central nervous system (CNS) development of invertebrates and mammals.
source: Biological timers play a key role in central nervous system (CNS) development of invertebrates and mammals, where a small pool of progenitors generates a vast amount of neuronal diversity (Grosskortenhaus et al., 2005; Isshiki et al., 2001; Kambadur et al., 1998; Kohwi and Doe, 2013; Kohwi et al., 2011; Li et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: In Drosophila, NBs delaminate from a ventral neuroectoderm at embryonic stages 9–11 to form an orthogonal two-dimensional grid with 30 NBs per hemi-segment.
source: In Drosophila, NBs delaminate from a ventral neuroectoderm at embryonic stages 9–11 to form an orthogonal two-dimensional grid with 30 NBs per hemi-segment.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Drosophila neuroblast development.

claim: Each NB undergoes asymmetric cell divisions every ~45 min to produce a series of ganglion mother cells (GMCs).
source: After formation, each NB undergoes asymmetric cell divisions every ~45 min to produce a series of ganglion mother cells (GMCs), each of which divides into two post-mitotic neurons.
evidence: This is established knowledge about NB division timing.

claim: Each GMC divides into two post-mitotic neurons.
source: After formation, each NB undergoes asymmetric cell divisions every ~45 min to produce a series of ganglion mother cells (GMCs), each of which divides into two post-mitotic neurons.
evidence: This is established knowledge about GMC division.

claim: The identity of each neuron is determined by the spatial position of the parental NB and by the TTF it inherits from the NB at the time of birth.
source: The identity of each neuron is determined by the spatial position of the parental NB and by the TTF it inherits from the NB at the time of birth (Doe, 2017; Kohwi and Doe, 2013; Pearson and Doe, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Temporal information is conveyed by the NB cell-intrinsic timer, which drives the sequential expression of four TTFs: Hunchback (Hb), Krüppel (Kr), Pdm (Flybase: Nubbin and Pdm2), and Castor (Cas).
source: Temporal information is therefore conveyed by the NB cell-intrinsic timer, which drives the sequential expression of four TTFs: Hunchback (Hb), Krüppel (Kr), Pdm (Flybase: Nubbin and Pdm2), and Castor (Cas) (Brody and Odenwald, 2000; Isshiki et al., 2001; Kambadur et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Hb expression is initiated by an external signal.
source: Hb expression is initiated by an external signal, but subsequent dynamics depends on cross-regulation between the TTFs themselves (Cleary and Doe, 2006; Grosskortenhaus et al., 2006; Isshiki et al., 2001; Tran et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Subsequent TTF dynamics depends on cross-regulation between the TTFs themselves.
source: Hb expression is initiated by an external signal, but subsequent dynamics depends on cross-regulation between the TTFs themselves (Cleary and Doe, 2006; Grosskortenhaus et al., 2006; Isshiki et al., 2001; Tran et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The orphan nuclear hormone receptor, Seven-up (Svp), is required to switch off Hb expression, but not for specifying early neuronal fates.
source: In addition, the orphan nuclear hormone receptor, Seven-up (Svp), is required to switch off Hb expression, but not for specifying early neuronal fates (Kanai et al., 2005; Kohwi et al., 2011; Mettler et al., 2006; Tran et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The TTF expression sequence is largely independent of the cell cycle.
source: The TTF expression sequence is largely independent of the cell cycle: some NBs undergo just one cell division during the Hb expression window, whereas others undergo two or three divisions (Baumgardt et al., 2009; Doe, 2017; Isshiki et al., 2001) indicating that cell division does not direct this temporal transition within the TTF cascade.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research and observational data.

claim: Some NBs undergo just one cell division during the Hb expression window, whereas others undergo two or three divisions.
source: The TTF expression sequence is largely independent of the cell cycle: some NBs undergo just one cell division during the Hb expression window, whereas others undergo two or three divisions (Baumgardt et al., 2009; Doe, 2017; Isshiki et al., 2001) indicating that cell division does not direct this temporal transition within the TTF cascade.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Cell division does not direct the temporal transition within the TTF cascade.
source: The TTF expression sequence is largely independent of the cell cycle: some NBs undergo just one cell division during the Hb expression window, whereas others undergo two or three divisions (Baumgardt et al., 2009; Doe, 2017; Isshiki et al., 2001) indicating that cell division does not direct this temporal transition within the TTF cascade.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that different numbers of divisions occur during the same TTF expression window.

claim: Mutations that arrest the cell cycle still allow normal TTF expression from Kr onward.
source: Consistent with that, mutations that arrest the cell cycle still allow normal TTF expression from Kr onward.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations of mutant phenotypes.

claim: NBs can undergo the entire expression sequence when cultured in isolation in vitro indicating TTF timer progression is independent of overall embryo development.
source: Also, NBs can undergo the entire expression sequence when cultured in isolation in vitro indicating TTF timer progression is independent of overall embryo development (Brody and Odenwald, 2002; Grosskortenhaus et al., 2005; Kambadur et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior experimental work.

claim: The TTF regulatory circuit contains backward interactions, whereby a TTF inhibits the expression of a TTF upstream in the cascade.
source: Examining the TTF regulatory circuit, however, we noted that in addition to these activator-relay interactions, the regulatory circuit includes two additional interaction types: backward interactions, whereby a TTF inhibits the expression of a TTF upstream in the cascade, and repressor-decay interactions, whereby an upstream regulator represses the expression of a downstream TTF (Figure 1A–B).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the regulatory circuit structure shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The TTF regulatory circuit contains repressor-decay interactions, whereby an upstream regulator represses the expression of a downstream TTF.
source: Examining the TTF regulatory circuit, however, we noted that in addition to these activator-relay interactions, the regulatory circuit includes two additional interaction types: backward interactions, whereby a TTF inhibits the expression of a TTF upstream in the cascade, and repressor-decay interactions, whereby an upstream regulator represses the expression of a downstream TTF (Figure 1A–B).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the regulatory circuit structure shown in Figure 1B.

claim: A model of the TTF timer that includes all experimentally described interactions can be captured by 17 independent parameters.
source: We formulated a model of the TTF timer that includes all experimentally described interactions, capturing their strengths by 17 independent parameters.
evidence: This is based on the computational model developed in the study.

claim: Main parameters in the TTF timer model include TTF degradation rates, TTF production rates, and the expression thresholds.
source: Main parameters in this model include TTF degradation rates, TTF production rates, and the expression thresholds defining the minimal TTF expression levels required for activating or repressing the controlled TTF and to confer neuronal identities (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes the structure of the computational model.

claim: A higher density of consistent circuits was observed in the region of repressor-decay timers.
source: We observed a higher density of consistent circuits in the region of repressor-decay timers.
evidence: This is based on computational screening of parameter space.

claim: The available data is not of sufficient resolution to distinguish whether the in vivo parameters progress the TTF timer through an activator-relay or a repressor-decay timer.
source: We conclude that the available data is not of sufficient resolution to distinguish whether the in vivo parameters progress the TTF timer through an activator-relay or a repressor-decay timer.
evidence: This is inferred from the analysis of existing experimental data.

claim: The time at which a protein decays between two thresholds is only moderately (logarithmically) sensitive to the values of these thresholds.
source: As we showed, the repressor-decay timer necessarily shows higher robustness under these conditions (Rappaport et al., 2005). The reason for this differential robustness is easily appreciated: the time at which a protein decays between two thresholds is only moderately (logarithmically) sensitive to the values of these thresholds (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by theoretical analysis and citation to prior work.

claim: The time to increase protein levels between two thresholds depends at least linearly, and typically significantly stronger, on thresholds values.
source: In contrast, the time to increase protein levels between two thresholds depends at least linearly, and typically significantly stronger, on thresholds values (Figure 2A–C)
evidence: This is based on theoretical analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: High robustness scores were found in the region of repressor-decay timers, while activator-relay timers were significantly less robust.
source: High robustness scores were found in the region of repressor-decay timers, while activator-relay timers were significantly less robust (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on computational analysis of robustness scores shown in the figures.

claim: Robust circuits are only found in a small region in the Kr-Hb sensitivity space, in which Pdm induction time is much more sensitive to Hb than to Kr deletion.
source: This analysis shows that robust circuits are only found in a small region in the Kr-Hb sensitivity space, in which Pdm induction time is much more sensitive to Hb than to Kr deletion.
evidence: This is based on computational analysis positioning circuits in sensitivity space.

claim: The consequences of TTF deletion and the removal of the respective interaction were tightly correlated.
source: As can be seen, the consequences of these two perturbations were tightly correlated, in particular when comparing the effect of deleting Kr to the removal of Kr-dependent regulation (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is based on computational analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: Following Pdm and Cas expression timing in mutant embryos has the power to inform about the robustness of the in vivo timer and about the relative contributions of the relay and decay regulations to the TTF progression.
source: We conclude that following Pdm and Cas expression timing in mutant embryos has the power to inform us not only about the robustness of the in vivo timer, but also about the relative contributions of the relay and decay regulations to the TTF progression.
evidence: This is inferred from the computational analysis of TTF deletion phenotypes.

claim: Pdm expression was longer than expected: about 180 min.
source: It further revealed that Pdm expression was longer than expected: about 180 min (Figure 4C), a time window that is long enough to generate more than the two previously reported Pdm +GMCs (Isshiki et al., 2001).
evidence: This is based on experimental measurements shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Pdm was upregulated when NB7-1 was producing the 4th GMC and downregulated after the NB generated the 7th GMC.
source: We found that Pdm was upregulated when NB7-1 was producing the 4th GMC and downregulated after the NB generated the 7th GMC (Figure 4E), indicating that four GMCs are produced within the Pdm expression window.
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Four GMCs are produced within the Pdm expression window.
source: We found that Pdm was upregulated when NB7-1 was producing the 4th GMC and downregulated after the NB generated the 7th GMC (Figure 4E), indicating that four GMCs are produced within the Pdm expression window.
evidence: This is inferred from the timing of Pdm expression relative to GMC production.

claim: A novel Kr+Pdm+ GMC was observed in the lineage, which was not previously reported.
source: Consistent with this finding, we observed a novel Kr+Pdm+ GMC in the lineage, which was not previously reported (Isshiki et al., 2001).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: Kr mutants did not alter Pdm induction timing.
source: We found that Kr mutants did not alter Pdm induction timing, whereas hb mutants advanced Pdm induction by about two cell-cycles (Figure 5A–C), showing that Pdm induction is more sensitive to deletion of the upstream repressor Hb.
evidence: This is based on experimental measurements shown in Figure 5.

claim: hb mutants advanced Pdm induction by about two cell-cycles.
source: We found that Kr mutants did not alter Pdm induction timing, whereas hb mutants advanced Pdm induction by about two cell-cycles (Figure 5A–C), showing that Pdm induction is more sensitive to deletion of the upstream repressor Hb.
evidence: This is based on experimental measurements shown in Figure 5.

claim: Pdm induction is more sensitive to deletion of the upstream repressor Hb.
source: We found that Kr mutants did not alter Pdm induction timing, whereas hb mutants advanced Pdm induction by about two cell-cycles (Figure 5A–C), showing that Pdm induction is more sensitive to deletion of the upstream repressor Hb.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data comparing mutant phenotypes.

claim: pdm mutants did not have as much effect on Cas induction as did Kr mutants.
source: Similarly, pdm mutants did not have as much effect on Cas induction as did Kr mutants, showing that Casinduction is more sensitive to deletion of the upstream repressor Kr rather than the upstream activator Pdm (Figure 5D–F).
evidence: This is based on experimental measurements shown in Figure 5.

claim: Cas induction is more sensitive to deletion of the upstream repressor Kr rather than the upstream activator Pdm.
source: Similarly, pdm mutants did not have as much effect on Cas induction as did Kr mutants, showing that Casinduction is more sensitive to deletion of the upstream repressor Kr rather than the upstream activator Pdm (Figure 5D–F).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data comparing mutant phenotypes.

claim: The in vivo circuit is in the region of robust timers that are dominated by repressor-decay interactions.
source: As can be seen, the in vivo circuit is in the region of robust timers that are dominated by repressor-decay interactions (Figure 5I).
evidence: This is based on positioning the in vivo circuit in the Decay-Relay space using experimental data.

claim: The timing of TTF expression is driven by a repressor-decay mechanism, rather than an activator-accumulation mechanism.
source: We therefore conclude that the timing of TTF expression is driven by a repressor-decay mechanism, rather than an activator-accumulation mechanism (Figure 5j).
evidence: This is the main conclusion based on all experimental and computational evidence.

claim: A repressor-decay timer drives the sequential TTF expression to generate stereotyped temporal fate specification in Drosophila embryonic NB lineages.
source: Our study suggests that a repressor-decay timer drives the sequential TTF expression to generate stereotyped temporal fate specification in Drosophila embryonic NB lineages (Figure 5J).
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study based on all evidence.

claim: A similar activator-relay mechanism was implicated in driving the TTF cascade in Drosophila optic lobe NB lineages.
source: A similar activator-relay mechanism was implicated also in driving the TTF cascade in Drosophila optic lobe NB lineages (Bertet et al., 2014; Li et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Kr induction was not included in the analysis since Kr was maintained in hb mutant embryos.
source: Kr induction was not included in this analysis since we found that Kr was maintained in hb mutant embryos (data not shown (Isshiki et al., 2001)), indicating that Kr is induced by a factor external to the cascade, similarly to Hb.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: Kr is induced by a factor external to the cascade, similarly to Hb.
source: Kr induction was not included in this analysis since we found that Kr was maintained in hb mutant embryos (data not shown (Isshiki et al., 2001)), indicating that Kr is induced by a factor external to the cascade, similarly to Hb.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Kr is maintained in hb mutants.

claim: Kr remained constitutively expressed in embryos which were forced to express constitutive levels of Hb.
source: Notably, Kr remained constitutively expressed in embryos which were forced to express constitutive levels of Hb.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: Hb affects Kr expression by determining shut-off time, allowing Kr decay only when Hb decays below a threshold.
source: Therefore, while Hb is an activator of Kr, it affects Kr expression not by determining its induction time but rather by determining shut-off time, allowing Kr decay only when Hb decays below a threshold, again implementing a repressor-decay, rather than an activator-relay timer.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations of Kr expression in Hb mutants and constitutive Hb expression.

claim: Hb is rapidly degraded during early embryogenesis, with an estimated half-life of ~15 min.
source: Hb is rapidly degraded during early embryogenesis, with an estimated half-life of ~15 min (Okabe-Oho et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Hb half-life is likely to be similarly short in NBs based on the 1:1 relationship between hb transcriptional activity and Hb protein levels.
source: While this half-life was not measured directly in NBs, it is likely to be similarly short based on the 1:1 relationship between hb transcriptional activity (detected with an intron probe) and Hb protein levels (detected with an antibody) (Grosskortenhaus et al., 2005).
evidence: This is inferred from cited experimental observations.

claim: Pdm starts expressing when Hb levels reduce to about 1–10% of their maximal value.
source: Assuming that Hb mRNA is similarly fast degrading, and that Hb is transcribed for only one cell-cycle, we estimate that Pdm starts expressing when Hb levels reduce to about 1–10% of their maximal value.
evidence: This is estimated based on known degradation rates and timing.

claim: The newly discovered Kr+Pdm+ GMC may produce an Eve-negative motor neuron, interneuron, or undergo programmed cell death.
source: The newly discovered GMC may produce an Eve-negative motor neuron, interneuron, or undergo programmed cell death (see Discussion).
evidence: This is speculation about the fate of the newly identified GMC.

claim: Six motor neurons have previously been reported for the NB7-1 lineage.
source: Six motor neurons have previously been reported for the NB7-1 lineage (Landgraf et al., 1997; Schmid et al., 1999), yet there are only five Eve + motor neurons in the lineage, raising the possibility that this 'new' GMC may produce an Eve-negative motor neuron.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: There are only five Eve+ motor neurons in the NB7-1 lineage.
source: Six motor neurons have previously been reported for the NB7-1 lineage (Landgraf et al., 1997; Schmid et al., 1999), yet there are only five Eve + motor neurons in the lineage, raising the possibility that this 'new' GMC may produce an Eve-negative motor neuron.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: Pdm is expressed in a burst during the Hb window.
source: Our analysis also revealed that Pdm is expressed in a burst during the Hb window. This was noted by Isshiki et al. (2001) but neither the functional significance nor the mechanism was discussed.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations in this study and prior work.

claim: Early Pdm expression may allow it to be inherited in the first-born GMC, where it is required to specify first-born GMC identity together with Hb.
source: Regarding function, we suggest that this early window of Pdm expression may allow it to be inherited in the first-born GMC, where in at least one lineage (NB4-2) it is required to specify first-born GMC identity, together with Hb (Bhat et al., 1995; Bhat and Schedl, 1994; McDonald et al., 2003; Yang et al., 1993; Yeo et al., 1995).
evidence: This is speculation supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Early Pdm and Cas expression is likely to be due to independent transcriptional activation of both genes, followed by repression of pdm transcription by Hb protein.
source: Regarding mechanism, early Pdm and Cas expression is likely to be due to independent transcriptional activation of both genes, followed by repression of pdm transcription by Hb protein (Kambadur et al., 1998).
evidence: This is speculation supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The Pdm protein produced from the initial transcriptional burst may persist into the new-born GMC.
source: The Pdm protein produced from the initial transcriptional burst, prior to Hb-mediated transcriptional repression, may persist into the new-born GMC.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of Pdm inheritance.

claim: There may be a mechanism for blocking Hb repression of pdm transcription specifically in early-forming NBs.
source: Alternatively, there may be a mechanism for blocking Hb repression of pdm transcription specifically in early-forming NBs.
evidence: This is speculation about an alternative mechanism.

claim: Repressor-decay dominating TTF progression was favored in evolution because it better buffers variation ('noise') in molecular parameters.
source: We propose that repressor-decay dominating TTF progression was favored in evolution because it better buffers variation ('noise') in molecular parameters.
evidence: This is speculation about evolutionary selection based on robustness analysis.

claim: Robust TTF progression is needed to maintain synchrony with the NB division cycles, a prerequisite for generating a reproducible NB lineage.
source: Robust TTF progression is needed to maintain synchrony with the NB division cycles, a prerequisite for generating a reproducible NB lineage.
evidence: This is inferred from the requirement for reproducible lineages.

claim: Activator accumulation requires continuous transcription while repressor degradation occurs following transcription shutdown.
source: First, activator accumulation requires continuous transcription while repressor degradation occurs following transcription shutdown.
evidence: This is based on the fundamental properties of the two mechanisms.

claim: Activator accumulation approaches some steady state, which limits the possible readout thresholds.
source: Second, activator accumulation approaches some steady state, which limits the possible readout thresholds.
evidence: This is based on the fundamental properties of accumulation dynamics.

claim: Most of the dynamics of activator accumulation is spent close to the steady-state threshold, so that small changes in threshold levels are translated into large changes in the measured delay time.
source: Furthermore, most of the dynamics is spent close to this threshold, so that small changes in threshold levels are translated into large changes in the measured delay time.
evidence: This is based on analysis of accumulation dynamics.

claim: There is no theoretical restriction on the readout threshold as a repressor decays to zero expression.
source: By contrast, there is no such (theoretical) restriction on the readout threshold as a repressor decays to zero expression.
evidence: This is based on the fundamental properties of decay dynamics.

claim: Encoding time-delays by repressor decay greatly promotes robustness.
source: Together, these properties lead to different buffering capacities, both when considering a single-step timer, and in the context of the full TTF timer model. In all cases, encoding time-delays by repressor decay greatly promotes robustness.
evidence: This is based on theoretical analysis and computational modeling.

claim: The hypothesis that robustness serves as an evolutionary-relevant selection pressure proved useful in defining the evolutionary selected circuit designs in multiple studies.
source: The hypothesis that robustness serves as an evolutionary-relevant selection pressure proved useful in defining the evolutionary selected circuit designs in multiple studies from our lab and from others (Alon et al., 1999; Barkai and Leibler, 1997; Eldar et al., 2002; Eldar et al., 2003; Gavish et al., 2016; Hart et al., 2014; Haskel-Ittah et al., 2012), and our current study further supports this notion.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The need to maintain robust gene expression timing within a noisy biological environment favored evolution of repressor-decay regulatory circuits controlling developmental patterning.
source: In conclusion, we propose that the need to maintain robust gene expression timing within a noisy biological environment favored evolution of repressor-decay regulatory circuits controlling developmental patterning.
evidence: This is the main proposal of the study based on all evidence.

claim: Robustness played a major role in the design of circuits that coordinate spatial patterning through the establishment of morphogen gradients or the control of direct cell-to-cell communication.
source: This was previously shown for circuits that coordinate spatial patterning through the establishment of morphogen gradients or the control of direct cell-to-cell communication (Barkai and Shilo, 2009; Eldar et al., 2002; Eldar et al., 2003; Gavish et al., 2016; Rahimi et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Robustness also played a major role in the design of developmental timers that function in neuronal differentiation.
source: Our study suggests that robustness also played a major role in the design of developmental timers that function in neuronal differentiation.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study.
